_readme: One entry per kind of equipment. Each one becomes a page at equipment/<id>/ and a QR label on equipment/labels.html. Models come from the current lab site and photos; set verify to false once someone has checked the entry against the real bench. Links starting with {{root}} point inside this site.

items.name: Oscilloscope
items.image_alt: The Agilent DSO6012A oscilloscope front panel
items.summary: Shows voltage over time. Use it to see a signal's shape, frequency and timing.
quick_start: Connect the probe to channel 1. Clip the ground lead to circuit ground, and only to ground.
Check the probe's attenuation switch. Lab probes are usually 10:1, and the channel's probe setting must match or every reading is off by 10x.
Press Default Setup, then AutoScale, for a starting picture.
Adjust volts per division and time per division until one or two periods fill the screen.
Move the trigger level into the signal's range so the waveform stops drifting.
Use Quick Meas for frequency, peak-to-peak and RMS instead of counting grid squares.
mistakes: AC coupling removes the DC part of a signal. Leave the channel on DC coupling unless you mean to hide an offset.
The ground clip is tied to earth ground through the scope's power cord. Clipping it to any node that is not ground shorts that node to earth.
If square waves look rounded or overshoot, compensate the probe on the scope's probe-comp output first.
A long ground lead rings on fast edges. Use the short ground spring when edges are fast.
safety: Do not measure mains voltage with a bench scope and a standard probe.

items.name: DC power supply
items.model: Agilent / Keysight E3647A, dual output, 60 W
items.image_alt: The Agilent E3647A dual-output power supply, with output 1 and output 2 terminals
items.summary: Two adjustable DC outputs with a current limit to protect your circuit.
quick_start: Turn the output off before connecting anything.
Pick the voltage range with the Low or High range key: up to 35 V at 0.8 A, or up to 60 V at 0.5 A.
Set the voltage first. Then set the current limit a little above what your circuit should draw.
Connect + to your supply rail and - to circuit ground. The separate green or earth terminal is chassis ground, not circuit ground.
Turn the output on and watch the current reading.
If the supply switches to CC (constant current), the circuit is drawing the full limit. Turn the output off and look for a short.
mistakes: Raising the current limit to make CC go away burns parts. CC means something is wrong.
Every supply and instrument in one circuit needs a shared ground connection.
The display shows one output at a time. Check which output you are adjusting before you turn the knob.
safety: Do not connect the two outputs in series or parallel unless the manual says how for this supply.

items.name: Function generator
items.model: Agilent / Keysight 33220A, 20 MHz function and arbitrary waveform
items.image_alt: The Agilent 33220A function generator, with its Output connector on the right
items.summary: Produces sine, square, ramp, pulse and arbitrary signals to drive a circuit.
quick_start: Pick the waveform, then set frequency, amplitude and offset.
Check the amplitude unit. It can be shown as Vpp, Vrms or dBm.
Set the output load (see below), then press Output to turn the signal on.
mistakes: The generator assumes a 50 ohm load by default. Into a high-impedance input, like a scope or most circuits, the real voltage is twice what the display says. In the Utility menu, open Output Setup and set the load to High Z so the display matches.
The output stays off until you press Output, even when the screen shows a waveform.

items.name: Digital multimeter
items.image_alt: The Fluke 45 dual-display multimeter, with V-ohm, 10 A, COM and 100 mA jacks
items.summary: Measures voltage, current, resistance and continuity, and can show two readings at once.
quick_start: Voltage: red lead in the V jack, black in COM, probes across the part (in parallel).
Current: move the red lead to the 100 mA jack (or 10 A for larger currents), then break the circuit and put the meter in series.
Resistance: power the circuit off first. For an exact value, lift one leg of the part out of the circuit.
Continuity: the meter beeps when the two probes are connected through a low resistance.
mistakes: A meter set to current is close to a short circuit. Putting it across a voltage source blows its fuse.
After measuring current, move the red lead back to the V jack.
Resistance readings on a powered circuit are wrong and can damage the meter.
safety: If a meter reads zero on current, the fuse may be blown. Report it rather than leaving it on the bench.

items.name: Soldering station
items.location: Soldering bench, under the fume hood
items.image_alt: The soldering bench with irons, a magnifier, a fume hood arm and parts trays
items.summary: For through-hole and surface-mount work on boards and wires.
quick_start: Turn on the ducted fume hood and put on eye protection.
Inspect the iron and cord for damage before you start.
Use the station's preset temperature unless you have a reason to change it.
Tin the tip: melt a little solder on it so it conducts heat well.
Heat the pad and the component lead together for a second or two, then feed solder into the joint, not onto the iron.
A good joint is shiny and shaped like a small cone. A dull ball means it needs more heat.
Put the iron back in its holder every time you let go of it, and switch it off when you are done.
mistakes: Carrying solder to the joint on the iron gives a cold joint. Heat the joint and let it melt the solder.
Holding the iron too long lifts pads off the board.
safety: Wear eye protection. Solder can spit.
Use the ducted hood to vent fumes.
Use rosin-free and lead-free solder whenever possible.
Keep cleaning solvents in their dispensing bottles.
Wash your hands with soap and water after soldering.
Never touch the hot parts of the iron, and never leave it lying on the bench.

items.name: 3D printers
items.image_alt: Two Prusa MK4 3D printers side by side on a bench
items.summary: Prints PLA enclosures, mounts and brackets for capstone projects. Watch your print live from your laptop.
quick_start: Slice your part in PrusaSlicer with the lab settings: MK4, 0.4 mm nozzle, PLA.
Read the full rules and settings on the 3D printing page before your first print.
mistakes: Changing speed or volume settings in the slicer. Leave them at the defaults.
safety: The nozzle and bed are hot. Keep hands out while the printer is moving.

links.label: 3D printing rules, settings and live video

items.name: PCB milling machine
items.image_alt: The LPKF ProtoMat S104 PCB milling machine under its clear cover, next to its control PC
items.summary: Turns your Gerber files into a single- or double-sided FR4 board. Operated by lab technicians only.
quick_start: Prepare TOP, BOT, DRL and BOA files, named as the PCB page explains.
Check them with the PCB file checker on this site.
Send them to a lab technician. Students do not run the machine.
mistakes: Expecting plated through-holes. The mill cannot make them; thread a wire through the hole instead.
Sending DXF instead of Gerber. DXF often imports corrupted.

links.label: PCB milling rules and file checker

items.name: Placement machine
items.image_alt: A manual pick-and-place machine with a blue arm over a copper board
items.summary: Helps place surface-mount parts accurately before reflow.
quick_start: Ask a lab technician before using it for the first time.

items.name: Reflow oven
items.image_alt: The LPKF ProtoFlow E reflow oven with heat-resistant gloves beside it
items.summary: Solders surface-mount boards. The largest board that fits is 8 x 6.5 in (203 x 165 mm).
quick_start: Ask a lab technician before using it for the first time.
mistakes: Designing a board larger than 8 x 6.5 in if you plan to reflow it here.
safety: Boards come out hot. Use the heat-resistant gloves.

items.name: Poster printer
items.image_alt: An HP large-format poster printer on a stand
items.summary: Free printing of capstone trifold posters. Email the PDF; pick it up in the technicians' office.
quick_start: Email your final PDF to the poster printing address with its dimensions.
Pick the print up in the technicians' office, usually within 2 days.
mistakes: Sending a draft. Only send the final version.

items.name: Lab computers and printer
items.image_alt: A Dell desktop with a monitor, keyboard and mouse on a lab bench
items.summary: Bench PCs for design tools, instrument control and programming boards.
quick_start: Sign in with your Northeastern account (TODO: confirm).
Save your work to your own cloud storage. Local files may be wiped.
For help with computers or software, go to the technicians' office or message a technician on Teams.
mistakes: Leaving files only on the desktop. Treat the bench PC as temporary.

items.name: Bench toolbox
items.model: One per bench, labeled with the bench number
items.image_alt: A black and yellow toolbox labeled Capstone 4
items.summary: The hand tools every bench should have. Put them back before you leave.
contents: Screwdriver set, 4 pieces, flat and Phillips
Hex key set, metric and inch, 30 pieces
Precision screwdriver set, 6 pieces, flat and Phillips
quick_start: Check the box against the list when you start. Report anything missing.

items.name: Shared tool cabinet
items.image_alt: A tall red rolling tool cabinet with many drawers
items.summary: Larger and less common tools, and lab supplies. Ask a technician.
quick_start: For tools and lab supplies, knock on the door at the technicians' office, or message a technician on Teams.

items.name: Battery charging stations
items.model: Hobby battery chargers on fire-resistant charging boxes
items.image_alt: Three battery chargers sitting on fire-resistant charging boxes, with charging leads and a printed rules sign
items.summary: Charge project batteries safely. Read the charger manual first.
quick_start: Read the charger's instruction manual before your first charge.
If you need a longer or balance-charging cable, ask the technicians.
safety: Do not modify, customize or alter any cables or connectors.
Do not leave batteries charging or connected over the weekend.
If you have any questions, go to the technicians' office for help.
